revision: 1. RESTRUCTURE LAYOUT FOR DATA INTEGRITY: Relocate the 'Recommended Actions' panel from its current overlapping position to the bottom-right corner, adjacent to the 'High-Risk Districts' list. Resize the 'Precipitation Intensity' chart to occupy the full width above this new position, ensuring all 12 months of rainfall data are fully visible and unobscured. 2. RESTORE LEGIBILITY: Increase the opacity of the Temperature Chart's X-axis labels to 100% white to ensure high contrast against the dark background. 3. UNIFY AESTHETIC WITH DISTINCTIVE ACCENTS: Remove the heavy drop shadow and solid background fill from the 'Recommended Actions' panel to align with the flat, grid-based editorial style. Instead, differentiate this section from data cards by using a subtle vertical rule or distinct border style. Replace generic blue square bullets with context-specific icons (e.g., gear, leaf) to provide visual variety and narrative distinction without breaking system consistency.
protected_strengths: High-contrast headline indicators at the top right for immediate metric comprehension.
Effective blue-to-red gradient in the temperature trend line communicating thermal shift.
Clear typographic hierarchy of headline indicators.
resolved_conflicts: Conflict: Occlusion of Rainfall Data vs. Text Legibility. Resolution: Moved text to bottom-right and resized chart to reveal all data, satisfying both Completeness and Simplicity mandates.

Conflict: Visual Consistency vs. Section Distinctiveness. Resolution: Removed 'floating card' styling (shadow/fill) to maintain Unity, but added specific icons and border rules to the Actions panel to ensure Variety and clear separation from data visualizations.
Conflict: Label Legibility vs. Dark Mode Aesthetic. Resolution: Increased label opacity to 100% white, prioritizing Information Density and Legibility over subtle background blending.
rationale: The revision prioritizes the non-negotiable requirement of visible data (Completeness) by physically separating the text and chart layers. It resolves the aesthetic conflict between Unity and Variety by adopting a consistent flat design system (Unity) while using semantic icons and structural rules (Variety) to distinguish narrative from data, ensuring the layout remains legible (Simplicity) and editorially distinct.
